findings.required_fix: Add tools/check_phase.py, docs/PHASES.md, docs/implementation-plan.md and docs/checks/phase-15.json to the phase-15 scope_evidence, and extend the phase-16/17 scope_evidence to the pinned sources, LICENSE, tools/test_portkey_access.py and docs/portkey-access-policies-research.md.

findings.description: The attempt-01 disposition ledger records only finding indices and a status: six entries of {review, finding: N, status: "implemented_pending_review"} with no statement of what changed or where the evidence is. The immediately preceding plan phase records a resolution sentence per finding (docs/phase-status.json:2307-2368, e.g. "PHASES and implementation plan link release plan."), and earlier phases add scope/evidence/acceptance_evidence. The plan requires 'disposition every advisory' (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:100) and AGENTS.md:5 requires the review artifact, checks, limitations and outcome to be recorded before advancing; as written a successor cannot audit any disposition without re-reading the full review text. I verified all six are in fact implemented, so this is a record-quality gap rather than an unimplemented fix.
findings.required_fix: Add a resolution string and evidence paths to each review_fixes entry (e.g. finding 0 -> source.json gitBlobSha1/bytes/sourceUrl/license/licenseNote plus tools/portkey-access.mjs:13-17; finding 1 -> whole-document delta at tools/portkey-access.mjs:32-45 and the difflib proof at tools/test_portkey_access.py:38-46; finding 2 -> contract.json:556-562 and tools/test_portkey_access.py:20-21), and record any limitations for this phase as phase 9 does at line 1817.

findings.description: The pin's provenance cross-checks are weaker than the convention this repository already established for a vendor pin. tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py:19-32 asserts a literal expected SHA-256 in the test file (a second anchor independent of source.json), asserts pin["commit"] appears in pin["sourceUrl"], re-derives licenseSha256 from the LICENSE bytes, and exercises the rejection path; lines 62-65 assert js-yaml in both tools/package.json and tools/package-lock.json, and tools/red-team-dataplane.mjs:16-19 checks the declared, locked and installed versions together. The Portkey verifier checks only the installed module version (line 18), and nothing asserts that openapi.yaml/LICENSE sourceUrls contain a27feb9 and parent.yaml's contains 8f91369, that pin.files has exactly the three expected keys (line 13 iterates whatever is present, so deleting an entry silently skips its digest check), or that licenseSha256 equals files.LICENSE.sha256. With no digest literal outside source.json, a consistent rewrite of both the YAML and the pin stays internally valid.
findings.required_fix: In tools/portkey-access.mjs add assertions that Object.keys(pin.files) equals exactly ['openapi.yaml','parent.yaml','LICENSE'], that each file's sourceUrl contains its governing commit (parent.yaml the parent, the others the commit), that pin.licenseSha256 === pin.files.LICENSE.sha256, and that tools/package.json dependencies and tools/package-lock.json both pin pin.yamlParser.version. Add the three expected SHA-256 literals to tools/test_portkey_access.py as an independent anchor.

findings.description: No test exercises any rejection path of tools/portkey-access.mjs, so its ten throw sites are unverified and a comparison that is accidentally always true would not be detected by the passing run alone. The repository convention does cover this: tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py:31-32 wraps verify_bytes in assertRaises after appending a byte, and tools/verify-contracts.py offers an explicit --self-test mode used by phases 1-8 and 12. Separately, the plan's operation table (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:20-26) and the expected mapping in test_portkey_access.py:22 are two independent hand-written copies of the same facts rather than cross-bound; phase 9's convention parses the plan table and compares it to the parsed operations (tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py:56-61), which catches plan/contract divergence.
findings.required_fix: Add a test that copies the pinned directory to a temporary tree, perturbs one input at a time (source.json digest, a spec route, a parent schema, the tag entry, the recorded addition count) and asserts node tools/portkey-access.mjs --check exits nonzero for each; and parse the five Method/Route rows out of docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:20-26 and assert they equal the verb/route pairs derived from contract.json.

findings.description: The whitespace criterion is satisfied only because the artifacts happened to be staged when the gate ran. git diff --check (line 72) compares the working tree to the index and sees nothing for staged-and-unmodified files, so the real coverage comes entirely from git diff --cached --check (line 73), which sees the additions only while they are in the index. Nothing in the gate asserts that the phase's artifacts are staged, so a rerun before staging reproduces exactly the vacuous pass attempt-01 identified (both commands recorded empty stdout at docs/checks/phase-15.json:27-28, 53-54, and docs/checks/phase-15.json itself is still untracked while docs/checks/phase-15-attempt-01.json is staged). I grepped the new plan, research and tooling files and found no trailing whitespace, so this is coverage fragility rather than a missed defect.
findings.required_fix: Add an assertion in tools/test_portkey_access.py that each phase-15 artifact is present in git ls-files --cached (or, alternatively, directly assert no trailing whitespace and a terminating newline over the plan, research, tooling and source.json/contract.json files) so the whitespace criterion cannot pass vacuously.

findings.description: The sole artifact phases 16 and 17 must extend is markedly denser than its sibling and has one unasserted semantic gap. tools/red-team-dataplane.mjs uses one statement per line with spaced operators and a multi-line guard (lines 16-25); tools/portkey-access.mjs packs a three-way digest comparison into lines 15-16, a two-part parameter-delta assertion into lines 30-31, and the entire contract construction with four nested object literals into a single 300-plus-character statement at line 47, with no blank lines anywhere. Separately, the plan describes the artifact as a 'normalized contract with all references resolved' (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:56-57, 96-98): all 18 $refs in contract.json do in fact resolve inside the artifact (I checked each against the 9 schemas and 4 parameters), but nothing asserts that closure, so a future re-extraction that drops a component would produce a dangling reference that only phase 16's fixtures would surface.
findings.required_fix: Reformat tools/portkey-access.mjs to one assertion per line with spaced operators and the contract literal built across multiple statements, matching tools/red-team-dataplane.mjs; and add a reference-closure assertion (walk contract.json for every "$ref" and require each '#/components/{schemas,parameters,securitySchemes}/NAME' target to exist in the extracted artifact) in the verifier or tools/test_portkey_access.py.

evidence: First-parent delta is now proved whole-document, not sampled: tools/portkey-access.mjs:32-45 clones the spec, deletes the two routes, nine schemas and AccessPolicyId parameter, removes exactly one 'Access Policies' tag (line 36, count asserted ===1) and the x-code-samples group with id 'access-policies' (lines 39-44), then requires isDeepStrictEqual(stripped, parent). Lines 25/27/31 additionally assert the added route, schema and parameter sets exactly, and line 30 asserts AccessPolicyId is absent from parent.components.parameters.

The +700/-0 claim is backed by a real line diff, not a count subtraction: tools/test_portkey_access.py:38-46 runs difflib.SequenceMatcher(autojunk=False) over parent.yaml and openapi.yaml and asserts (added, removed) == (700, 0); tools/portkey-access.mjs:46 independently requires the line-count difference to equal pin.additions with pin.deletions === 0 (source.json:37-38).

I corroborated the delta independently: grep for 'Access Policies|access-policies|policies/access|AccessPolicy' returns 0 matches in contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/parent.yaml and matches in openapi.yaml at lines 139 (tag), 20003 and 20244 (routes), 20007-20402 (operations and samples), 23688 (AccessPolicyId) and 41307-41308 (navigation group) - exactly the five regions the verifier removes.

The pin now matches the repository vendor convention: contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/source.json:6-39 records per-file sha256, gitBlobSha1, bytes and sourceUrl for openapi.yaml, parent.yaml and LICENSE, plus schemaVersion, license MIT, licensePath/licenseSha256, yamlParser js-yaml 4.3.2, redistributed, usedForGeneration, retrievedAt, additions/deletions and an explicit licenseNote recording that the retained MIT text carries an OpenAI copyright (LICENSE:1-3). tools/portkey-access.mjs:12-18 asserts the commit/parent literals, recomputes sha256, byte length and git blob SHA-1 for every pinned file, and rejects js-yaml drift against tools/package.json:11.

The security scheme is now in the machine-checked extraction and bound by test: contract.json:556-562 carries components.securitySchemes['Portkey-Key'] = {apiKey, in: header, name: x-portkey-api-key}; tools/portkey-access.mjs:47 extracts it (so the whole-document comparison at line 45 also proves it unchanged from the parent) and line 49 asserts all five operations declare security [{Portkey-Key: []}]; tools/test_portkey_access.py:20-21 asserts the exact apiKey/header/x-portkey-api-key triple.

The gate suite now pins contract substance, not prose: tools/test_portkey_access.py:22-36 asserts the five verb-to-route-to-operationId pairs and per-operation security, the exact set of twelve query parameter names (resolving $refs through components.parameters), maxLength 36/36/100/64/255 for user_id/agent_id/server_id/search/created_by, page_size and current_page each exactly {type: integer, minimum: 0}, and required sets {name, subjects, targets} for CreateAccessPolicyRequest and {version, subjects, targets} for UpdateAccessPolicyRequest.

Every plan claim I sampled verifies against contract.json: name minLength 1 / maxLength 64 (724-725), description nullable maxLength 256 (728-732), subjects/targets minItems 1 (743, 750), version minimum 1 (771), MCP target requires type/server_id/tools (635-639) while provider requires only type/provider_id (674-677), tools/models each oneOf ALL-enum or array with minItems 1 and items minLength 1 (651-707), create-effect inference and the allow-subject rule in the endpoint prose (line 21), update preserving stored name/description/effect/enabled (413), PUT and DELETE returning bare {type: object} (457, 518), and no required list on AccessPolicy (811-884) or AccessPolicyListItem (885-961) or the list envelope (291-309).

The plan's 'both default response modes produce the same data' claim holds: the only 'default' keyword in the entire extracted family is CreateAccessPolicyRequest.enabled: true (contract.json:755-758), which is request-side, so the response family declares no defaults.

The authentication premise is implemented, not assumed: crates/scm-sdk/src/auth.rs:801-805 shows Credentials::RuntimeKey validating the key and inserting x-portkey-api-key via sensitive_header, and lines 735-745 reject any caller-supplied authorization/x-pan-token/x-payload-hash/x-portkey-api-key/x-tsg-id header, which is exactly the 'never silently rewrite credentials' and 'reject OAuth, scan and anonymous clients' basis the plan relies on (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:37-45).

The checks were executed against the reviewed source: docs/checks/phase-15.json:2-6 records phase 15, source_sha256 75b6b6c1c424961f4038836a176cf720e94afd0a43f8e5d25f668d48bbc53676 (identical to the reviewed fingerprint), source_unchanged true and passed true; the six recorded command arrays equal tools/check_phase.py:72-77 commands_for(15) element for element with exit_code 0 and real captured output (the verifier printed the five operations with Portkey-Key and schemas:9; 30 review-gate and 5 Portkey tests ran). tools/review_phase.py:99-113 enforces precisely that equality, and lines 43-60 hash git ls-files --cached --others so the untracked/staged artifacts are inside the fingerprint.

'No SDK implementation' is machine-enforced: tools/test_portkey_access.py:53-59 requires an empty git diff --name-only against release baseline b65f3c98218f32e836bbdcc0bd95614e9836a4e6 and no untracked files for Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/scm-sdk, LICENSE and NOTICE while active_phase is 15; the baseline matches the plan's recorded release baseline (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:18) and the current HEAD commit b65f3c9.

All six attempt-01 findings are actually implemented, not merely marked: provenance fields and licenseNote (source.json:9-39), whole-document delta plus real diff (portkey-access.mjs:32-46, test_portkey_access.py:38-46), securitySchemes in the contract with an asserted header (contract.json:556-562, test_portkey_access.py:20-21), scope_evidence expanded to nine artifacts and the research document linked from the plan (docs/phase-status.json:3196-3206, docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:166), artifacts staged so git diff --cached --check is non-vacuous with only the upstream YAMLs excluded (check_phase.py:72-73), and parameter/bounds/mapping assertions added (test_portkey_access.py:18-36).

Phase registration is complete and consistent: docs/PHASES.md:78-86 describes phases 15-17 and links the plan, docs/implementation-plan.md:160-164 records the maintainer authorization of the a27feb9 delta through phases 15-17, docs/phase-status.json:3190-3269 registers all three phases with the plan path, and docs/phase-status.json:3271 sets active_followup_plan. tools/review_phase.py:145-153 verified all predecessor gates before this review was issued.

The verify-contracts.py result in this gate is pre-existing behavior, not a new regression: the plain invocation reports extractedBaselineVerified false in docs/checks/phase-02.json:47, phase-05.json:47, phase-07.json:47, phase-11.json:212, phase-90.json:132, phase-92.json:480 and phase-15.json:84 alike, while only the --baseline .local/typescript variant reports true; phase 15, like phases 9 and 13, registers only the plain invocation.

The narrowed gate is measurable against precedent: tools/check_phase.py:188-191 (phase 9) and 89-91 (phase 13) both include tools/test_ci.py, and tools/test_ci.py:380-385, 44-63, 396-410 and 412-416 assert about tools/check_phase.py's timeout budget, workflow wiring, contracts subset and vendor exclusion pathspec; commands_for(15) at lines 72-77 omits it, and tools/test_review_phase.py:20-24 pins only phases 1-8.
limitations: Read-only tools and no network: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint 75b6b6c1, the recorded checks digest df8048f7, or any file SHA-256/git blob SHA-1; re-execute tools/portkey-access.mjs; or re-run the unittest suites. I verified that the recorded command list equals commands_for(15), that the recorded source_sha256 matches the reviewed fingerprint, and that the captured outputs are internally consistent with the code they came from, but the executions themselves are taken from docs/checks/phase-15.json.

Upstream identity of the vendored bytes cannot be established from inside the repository. source.json now records gitBlobSha1 and per-file sourceUrl, which makes the pin verifiable against the upstream git objects in principle, but nothing available offline proves that openapi.yaml and parent.yaml are the real Portkey-AI/openapi blobs at a27feb9 and 8f91369.

I could not run git, so I could not diff tools/check_phase.py, docs/PHASES.md or docs/implementation-plan.md against HEAD to confirm the changes are purely additive, nor confirm directly that the phase artifacts were staged at the moment the gate ran. I inferred additivity from the passing phases-1-8 command-contract hash (tools/test_review_phase.py:20-24) and staging from the recorded empty git diff --cached --check output combined with the deliberate YAML exclusion pathspec, which would be pointless for untracked files.

The whole-document delta proof operates on parsed YAML, so comment, key-ordering and anchor changes are invisible to it; the difflib proof of (700 added, 0 removed) in tools/test_portkey_access.py covers the textual dimension. Together these are strong, but I did not separately re-derive a byte-level diff myself.

Judgment of the plan's implementation design (client construction rules, replay policy, validator semantics, Patch/Optional choices) is necessarily a paper review; its correctness can only be confirmed by phase 16's fixtures. I raised no finding on the stricter-than-schema client validations (rejecting group ANY, requiring a specific subject for allow) because they are derived from the upstream endpoint prose at contract.json:21 and the plan states explicitly that no client authorization decision is inferred from them.

Per the review scope I did not re-audit phases 1-14 infrastructure, the frozen TypeScript baseline, or the 0.2.0/0.1.1 release evidence; I examined phase 9 and phase 13 only as the directly comparable plan-phase precedents for gate scope, scope_evidence and disposition bookkeeping.
